# Research question and role of this dataset

**Hypothesis:** Between January 2002 and December 2023, countries with a higher GDP had fewer commercial flight accidents per million departures than countries with a lower GDP.

This file prepares the **denominator** of that rate: annual commercial flight departures by country. Accident counts and GDP are merged in a later stage.

The data come from the World Bank's World Development Indicators, indicator **IS.AIR.DPRT, "Air transport, registered carrier departures worldwide"**. It counts the domestic takeoffs and the takeoffs abroad made by air carriers registered in each country. The underlying source is ICAO, *Civil Aviation Statistics of the World*, plus ICAO staff estimates. One departure is one flight stage, from takeoff to the next landing.

# Data import


```{r import}
raw_file <- "API_IS.AIR.DPRT_DS2_en_csv_v2_30814.csv"
out_dir  <- "output"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# The first 4 lines are World Bank metadata 
readLines(raw_file, n = 3, encoding = "UTF-8")

raw <- read.csv(raw_file, skip = 4, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
# Drop the empty column created by the trailing comma on every line
raw <- raw[, names(raw) != "" & !grepl("^V[0-9]+$", names(raw))]
dim(raw)
range(as.integer(names(raw)[-(1:4)]))
```

The raw file has `r nrow(raw)` rows (entities) and annual columns from 1960 to 2025.

# Data cleaning

## Step 1: Remove regional, income and lending aggregates

The World Bank file mixes individual economies with groups such as "World", "High income" and "Sub-Saharan Africa". These are sums of country rows and would double-count departures.

```{r aggregates}
aggregates <- c("AFE","AFW","ARB","CEB","CSS","EAP","EAR","EAS","ECA","ECS","EMU","EUU",
                "FCS","FCV","HIC","HPC","IBD","IBT","IDA","IDB","IDX","INX","LAC","LCN",
                "LDC","LIC","LMC","LMY","LTE","MEA","MIC","MNA","NAC","OED","OSS","PRE",
                "PSS","PST","SAS","SSA","SSF","SST","TEA","TEC","TLA","TMN","TSA","TSS",
                "UMC","WLD")
is_agg <- raw$`Country Code` %in% aggregates
sum(is_agg)                      # aggregate rows removed
raw$`Country Name`[is_agg]       # what was removed
countries <- raw[!is_agg, ]
nrow(countries)                  # economies kept
```

## Step 2: Restrict to the study period


```{r period}
years <- as.character(2002:2023)
countries <- countries[, c("Country Name", "Country Code", years)]
```

## Step 3: Reshape to long format, handle missing values, validate and round

Blank cells become `NA` ("not reported"), not zero. Nothing is imputed. Fractional values are ICAO estimates and are rounded to whole flights.

```{r reshape}
long <- data.frame(
  `Country Name` = rep(countries$`Country Name`, times = length(years)),
  `Country Code` = rep(countries$`Country Code`, times = length(years)),
  Year           = rep(as.integer(years), each = nrow(countries)),
  Departures     = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(unlist(countries[, years], use.names = FALSE))),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

n_cells      <- nrow(long)
n_nonmissing <- sum(!is.na(long$Departures))
n_fractional <- sum(!is.na(long$Departures) & long$Departures %% 1 != 0)
n_negative   <- sum(long$Departures < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
c(cells = n_cells, non_missing = n_nonmissing, fractional = n_fractional, negative = n_negative)

long$Departures[!is.na(long$Departures) & long$Departures < 0] <- NA
long$Departures <- round(long$Departures)
long$Departures_millions <- long$Departures / 1e6

coverage <- tapply(!is.na(long$Departures), long$`Country Code`, sum)
long$Years_reported_2002_2023 <- as.integer(coverage[long$`Country Code`])
long <- long[order(long$`Country Name`, long$Year), ]
```

Of `r fmt(n_cells)` country-year cells, `r fmt(n_nonmissing)` hold a value. `r n_fractional` of those (`r round(n_fractional / n_nonmissing * 100, 1)`%) were fractional ICAO estimates and were rounded. `r n_negative` negative values were found.

## Step 4: Save the cleaned data

```{r save}
write.csv(long, file.path(out_dir, "departures_clean_long_2002_2023.csv"), row.names = FALSE, na = "")
wide <- reshape(long[, c("Country Name", "Country Code", "Year", "Departures")],
                idvar = c("Country Name", "Country Code"), timevar = "Year",
                direction = "wide", sep = "_")
names(wide) <- sub("^Departures_", "", names(wide))
write.csv(wide, file.path(out_dir, "departures_clean_wide_2002_2023.csv"), row.names = FALSE, na = "")
```

# Coverage and completeness

```{r coverage}
cov_table <- data.frame(
  Coverage  = c("All 22 years", "15 or more years", "10 to 21 years", "1 to 9 years", "No data"),
  Countries = c(sum(coverage == 22), sum(coverage >= 15), sum(coverage >= 10 & coverage < 22),
                sum(coverage >= 1 & coverage < 10), sum(coverage == 0)))
cov_table$Share_pct <- round(cov_table$Countries / length(coverage) * 100, 1)
cov_table

cname <- tapply(long$`Country Name`, long$`Country Code`, `[`, 1)
sort(cname[names(coverage)[coverage == 0]], method = "radix")     # no data
low <- coverage[coverage >= 1 & coverage < 10]
setNames(as.integer(low), cname[names(low)])                      # fewer than 10 years

d <- long[!is.na(long$Departures), ]
d[d$Departures == 0, c("Country Name", "Year")]                   # zero-departure years
```

# Descriptive statistics

Skewness and excess kurtosis use the adjusted sample estimators (G1, G2), the same as SPSS and Excel. Quartiles use R's default method (type 7).

```{r functions}
skew_g1 <- function(x) { n <- length(x); m <- mean(x); s <- sd(x)
  n / ((n - 1) * (n - 2)) * sum(((x - m) / s)^3) }
kurt_g2 <- function(x) { n <- length(x); m <- mean(x); s <- sd(x)
  n * (n + 1) / ((n - 1) * (n - 2) * (n - 3)) * sum(((x - m) / s)^4) -
    3 * (n - 1)^2 / ((n - 2) * (n - 3)) }
describe <- function(x) c(N = length(x), Total = sum(x), Mean = mean(x), Median = median(x),
  SD = sd(x), Min = min(x), Q1 = unname(quantile(x, .25)), Q3 = unname(quantile(x, .75)),
  Max = max(x), Skewness = skew_g1(x), Kurtosis = kurt_g2(x))
```

## Pooled distribution (all country-years)

```{r pooled}
pooled <- rbind(Raw   = describe(d$Departures),
                Log10 = describe(log10(d$Departures[d$Departures > 0])))
write.csv(round(pooled, 2), file.path(out_dir, "stats_pooled.csv"))
round(t(pooled), 2)
```

```{r hist, fig.height=4}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
hist(d$Departures / 1e6, breaks = 60, col = "grey70", border = "white",
     main = "Raw scale", xlab = "Departures per country-year (millions)")
hist(log10(d$Departures[d$Departures > 0]), breaks = 40, col = "steelblue", border = "white",
     main = "Log10 scale", xlab = "log10(departures)")
```

The raw distribution is extremely right-skewed: the mean (`r fmt(pooled["Raw", "Mean"])`) is about `r round(pooled["Raw", "Mean"] / pooled["Raw", "Median"])` times the median (`r fmt(pooled["Raw", "Median"])`), with skewness `r round(pooled["Raw", "Skewness"], 1)`. On the log10 scale skewness is `r round(pooled["Log10", "Skewness"], 2)` and kurtosis `r round(pooled["Log10", "Kurtosis"], 2)`, close to normal. Use log(departures) in parametric tests and medians to describe groups.

## By year

```{r by-year}
by_year <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, d$Year), function(g)
  data.frame(Year = g$Year[1], t(describe(g$Departures)),
             Top_country = g$`Country Name`[which.max(g$Departures)], check.names = FALSE)))
by_year$YoY_change_total_pct <- c(NA, diff(by_year$Total) / head(by_year$Total, -1) * 100)
num <- sapply(by_year, is.numeric); by_year[num] <- round(by_year[num], 1)
write.csv(by_year, file.path(out_dir, "stats_by_year.csv"), row.names = FALSE, na = "")
rownames(by_year) <- NULL
by_year[, c("Year", "N", "Total", "Mean", "Median", "SD", "Max", "YoY_change_total_pct")]
```

```{r trend-plot}
par(mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
plot(by_year$Year, by_year$Total / 1e6, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2,
     ylim = c(0, 40), xlab = "Year", ylab = "Departures (millions)",
     main = "Total registered-carrier departures, reporting countries")
rect(2019.5, -5, 2021.5, 45, col = adjustcolor("grey", 0.25), border = NA)
text(2020.5, 39, "COVID-19", cex = 0.85)
grid(nx = NA, ny = NULL)
```

Totals are sums across the countries reporting in each year (`r min(by_year$N)` to `r max(by_year$N)`), so part of the 2010 rise reflects more countries reporting. Departures rose `r round((by_year$Total[by_year$Year == 2019] / by_year$Total[by_year$Year == 2002] - 1) * 100)`% from 2002 to 2019, fell `r abs(round(by_year$YoY_change_total_pct[by_year$Year == 2020]))`% in 2020, and reached `r round(by_year$Total[by_year$Year == 2023] / by_year$Total[by_year$Year == 2019] * 100)`% of the 2019 level by 2023.

## By country

```{r by-country}
grand_total <- sum(d$Departures)
by_country <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, d$`Country Code`), function(g) {
  g <- g[order(g$Year), ]; x <- g$Departures
  first <- g[1, ]; last <- g[nrow(g), ]; span <- last$Year - first$Year
  data.frame(`Country Name` = g$`Country Name`[1], `Country Code` = g$`Country Code`[1],
    Years_reported = length(x), First_year = first$Year, Last_year = last$Year,
    Total_departures = sum(x), Mean_annual = mean(x), Median_annual = median(x),
    SD = if (length(x) > 1) sd(x) else NA,
    CV_pct = if (length(x) > 1 && mean(x) > 0) sd(x) / mean(x) * 100 else NA,
    Min = min(x), Max = max(x),
    CAGR_pct = if (span > 0 && first$Departures > 0)
      ((last$Departures / first$Departures)^(1 / span) - 1) * 100 else NA,
    Share_of_period_total_pct = sum(x) / grand_total * 100, check.names = FALSE)
}))
by_country <- by_country[order(-by_country$Total_departures), ]
num <- sapply(by_country, is.numeric); by_country[num] <- round(by_country[num], 2)
write.csv(by_country, file.path(out_dir, "stats_by_country.csv"), row.names = FALSE, na = "")
rownames(by_country) <- NULL

head(by_country[, c("Country Name", "Mean_annual", "Share_of_period_total_pct", "CAGR_pct")], 10)
summary(by_country$Mean_annual)
c(top10_share_pct = sum(head(by_country$Share_of_period_total_pct, 10)),
  countries_under_10k = sum(by_country$Mean_annual < 10000),
  countries_over_1M   = sum(by_country$Mean_annual > 1e6))
```

```{r top-plot, fig.height=5}
top15 <- head(by_country, 15)
par(mar = c(4.5, 10, 3, 1))
barplot(rev(top15$Mean_annual / 1e6), names.arg = rev(top15$`Country Name`), horiz = TRUE,
        las = 1, col = c(rep("grey70", 14), "steelblue"), border = NA,
        xlab = "Mean annual departures (millions)", main = "15 largest countries, 2002–2023")
```

# Data-quality screen

Year-on-year changes larger than 100% (up or down) are flagged for review. They mark pandemic effects, a carrier starting or stopping, or breaks in reporting.

```{r flags}
lo   <- long[order(long$`Country Code`, long$Year), ]
prev <- ave(lo$Departures, lo$`Country Code`, FUN = function(v) c(NA, head(v, -1)))
yoy  <- (lo$Departures / prev - 1) * 100
flag <- !is.na(yoy) & prev > 0 & abs(yoy) > 100
flags <- data.frame(`Country Name` = lo$`Country Name`[flag], Year = lo$Year[flag],
                    Previous_year = prev[flag], Departures = lo$Departures[flag],
                    YoY_change_pct = round(yoy[flag], 1), check.names = FALSE)
write.csv(flags, file.path(out_dir, "flag_large_yoy_changes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

c(flagged = nrow(flags), in_2020_2022 = sum(flags$Year %in% 2020:2022),
  prior_year_10k_plus = sum(flags$Previous_year >= 10000))
flags[flags$Previous_year >= 10000, ]
```

The largest break is Canada, from `r fmt(flags$Previous_year[flags$"Country Name" == "Canada" & flags$Year == 2003])` departures in 2002 to `r fmt(flags$Departures[flags$"Country Name" == "Canada" & flags$Year == 2003])` in 2003, most likely a change in reporting coverage rather than real growth.
